details: Encloses exp(w * Log(z)) over complete input rectangles.
Exact signed integer powers retain their algebraic domain.
Zero bases require a positive, exactly-real exponent enclosure; other noninteger powers exclude zero and retain the principal logarithm cut.
Original base and exponent subexpressions remain evaluated before trivial outer cases.
The real evaluator and Python complex evalf surface are unchanged.
Preserves the original Eq owner and typed coordinate identity.
Intersects the generated family with the requested domain before imposing original-source definedness.
Unknown definedness remains a ConditionSet over the complete family; an invalid or cancelled source cannot be silently discarded.
This is deliberately conservative for some meromorphic sources.
Prime-power valuations, odd-unit group equations, noncyclic two-adic units and CRT generate complete sets, including nonunits.
An independent count theorem, factor-map validation, reference modular exponentiation and canonical sorted-distinct checks reject incomplete or forged sets.
The native APIs take u64 moduli and positive u64 degrees.
Public degree two preserves existing sqrt_mod selection; 79 modulo 105 selects 38, with complete roots [17,32,38,52,53,67,73,88].
The public API observes one captured active request across both native phases and result publication; first Python refusals remain terminal.
This is an independent same-crate in-process checker, not a portable proof-kernel certificate.

bounds_and_limitations: At most 65,536 materialized roots; nontrivial native scalar queries currently share that bound.
At most 65,536 entries in odd-group logarithm tables. For example, cubic roots of 8 modulo 4294967311 explicitly refuse although roots exist.
Native generation and verification have separate fixed 256,000,000 work and 64 MiB allocation ceilings; both debit the same captured active Python request.
Existing bounded synchronous factorization and specialized square-root helpers reserve work and observe cancellation at their boundaries, not inside every helper instruction.
Principal complex arithmetic retains intrinsic preflight bounds; no new caller-owned budget or cancellation guarantee is claimed for that API.
No compatibility-profile promotion, portable-certificate claim, performance claim or broad workstream closure.
